Prepare observed steps for analytically normalised movement kernels

Source: R/exact.R
prepare_ssf_steps.Rd

No controls or proposal weights are required. Each row is one positive observed step, and each ID is an uninterrupted independent segment. Directional target effects require the target bearing relative to the previous heading, chosen at the step origin before observing the endpoint. The constructor can derive this from target_bearing and previous_bearing. It cannot establish from numbers alone how a supplied target was chosen.

Usage

prepare_ssf_steps(
  data,
  density_measure,
  id = "ID",
  time = NULL,
  expected_interval = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with ID, step and angle columns. Angles are radians. Optional relative_target_bearing, or target_bearing and previous_bearing, describes the prospective target direction. Optional target_active is logical; FALSE removes its directional effect when direction is undefined.

density_measure

Required: area or step_angle. This determines the reference measure of the exact likelihood, not an importance proposal.

id

Name of the independent segment column.

time

Optional numeric or POSIXct time column.

expected_interval

Optional positive interval between consecutive observations in a segment, in seconds for POSIXct times.

Value

An ssf_steps data frame with canonical covariates and metadata.
